The authors suggest that interneuron dysfunction may contribute to cognitive deficits in schizophrenia by disrupting this long-range synchrony.

entities.name: Persistent (delay) activity
entities.summary: Firing that continues through the delay of a memory task. In monkeys, neurons of prefrontal cortex and of the thalamic nucleus medialis dorsalis change their firing during the delay of a delayed-response test, some staying above their intertrial rate throughout, and most delay activity around the principal sulcus is directional, tuned to the remembered cue location. In monkey dorsolateral PFC it depends on NR2B NMDA receptors; dopamine D1 stimulation sculpts it along an inverted U (monkey), and α2A-adrenoceptor stimulation strengthens it (monkeys and rats). In mice, medial prefrontal neurons with elevated delay spiking, absent on error trials, need mediodorsal thalamic input to sustain it. Whether sustained spiking is what holds the memory is debated: in monkey PFC, brief gamma and beta bursts accompany encoding and readout, and their authors argue that working memory is manifested by discrete oscillatory dynamics and spiking, not sustained activity.

entities.name: Mixed selectivity & population dynamics
entities.summary: Single prefrontal neurons respond to mixtures of task variables. In monkeys performing an object sequence memory task, such mixed-selectivity neurons carried distributed information about all task-relevant aspects, giving high-dimensional representations whose dimensionality collapsed on error trials. In monkeys trained to flexibly select and integrate noisy sensory inputs towards a choice, the complex responses of single prefrontal neurons were understood as one population dynamical process, reproduced by a trained recurrent neural network, suggesting that selection and integration happen within the same circuits.

entities.name: Rule coding
entities.summary: In monkeys trained to apply two abstract rules (same or different) to new pictures, the most prevalent prefrontal activity coded the rule in effect. In mice using two rules to guide attention, prefrontal rule representations were sustained by mediodorsal thalamic input, which amplified local prefrontal connectivity so that rule-specific neural sequences emerged, without relaying categorical information. Theory proposes that actively maintained prefrontal representations of goals and the means to achieve them provide bias signals that guide processing elsewhere in the brain.

entities.name: Prefrontal rhythms & synchrony
entities.summary: Inhibiting parvalbumin interneurons suppresses gamma oscillations in mouse neocortex, and driving them generates gamma rhythmicity. Correlated firing and 4–12 Hz theta coupling between hippocampal CA1 and medial PFC strengthen during spatial working memory (rat), and in mice gamma-frequency synchrony between hippocampus and PFC appears to mediate the encoding of spatial cues. Theta synchrony between medial PFC and basolateral amygdala rises in mice that tell safety from danger. In monkeys, frontal–parietal synchrony is stronger at lower frequencies during top-down and at higher frequencies during bottom-up attention, and in PFC brief gamma bursts accompany the encoding and re-activation of working-memory content, while beta bursts mark a default state interrupted by encoding and decoding.

entities.name: Value coding
entities.summary: During economic choice, monkey orbitofrontal neurons encode the value of offered and chosen goods independently of visuospatial factors and motor responses, so OFC neurons seem to be a good candidate network for the value assignment underlying choice. In humans, ventromedial PFC encodes the values of specific options during comparative choice, whereas the anterior cingulate cortex encodes the average value of the foraging environment and the cost of foraging.

entities.name: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
entities.summary: Lateral prefrontal cortex of primates, around the principal sulcus (area 46). In monkeys, most of its neurons with delay activity are tuned to the direction of a remembered cue, and their persistent firing depends on NR2B NMDA receptors. Damage to lateral prefrontal cortex (Brodmann's area 9) in marmosets causes a loss of inhibitory control in attentional selection. In schizophrenia, its blood flow fails to rise during the Wisconsin Card Sort and its deep layer 3 pyramidal neurons have a lower dendritic spine density, and a review concludes that its parvalbumin interneurons make less GABA (human).

entities.name: Orbitofrontal cortex
entities.summary: During economic choice, its neurons encode the value of offered and chosen goods (monkey). Surgical removal of orbital prefrontal cortex attenuated reinforcer-devaluation effects and impaired object reversal learning, but excitotoxic, fiber-sparing lesions confined to OFC altered neither reversal learning nor fear of snakes, and a reported loss of inhibitory control was traced to damage to nearby fiber tracts; those authors argue for a more specialized role in reward-guided behavior that includes value updating (monkey). In marmosets, OFC damage causes a loss of inhibitory control in affective processing. Theory proposes that OFC provides a map of the current task state used for reinforcement learning. In monkeys, the amygdala connects most densely with posterior orbitofrontal and posterior medial prefrontal cortex.

entities.name: Anterior cingulate cortex
entities.summary: In the Stroop task, its conflict-related activity predicts greater prefrontal activity and adjustments in behavior (human). During foraging, it encodes the average value of the environment and the cost of foraging (human). Theory proposes that the dorsal ACC allocates cognitive control according to its expected value. In monkeys, cingulate area 24 sends comparatively more projections to the amygdala than it receives.

entities.name: Subgenual cingulate cortex (area 25)
entities.summary: Metabolically overactive in treatment-resistant depression. Chronic deep brain stimulation of the white matter tracts next to it was associated with striking and sustained remission in four of six patients with refractory depression, along with reduced local blood flow and changes in downstream limbic and cortical sites (human). In monkeys, area 25 sends comparatively more projections to the amygdala than it receives.

entities.name: Medial prefrontal cortex (rodent)
entities.summary: In rats and mice, the medial prefrontal areas, which include the prelimbic and infralimbic cortices; their names and borders differ between rodent atlases, and researchers disagree on the terms. In mice, spatial working memory relies on its circuits: inhibiting its somatostatin interneurons or its direct hippocampal input during cue encoding, or its mediodorsal thalamic input during maintenance, impairs the task. Medial frontal lesions selectively impair attentional set shifting, as prefrontal lesions do in primates (rat). Activating its neurons that project to the dorsal raphe has a profound, rapid and reversible effect on the selection of active behavior in a challenging situation (rat), raising or lowering synaptic strength in dorsal mPFC moves social rank up or down (mouse), and its theta input entrains the basolateral amygdala when mice recognize safety. Inhibiting ventral hippocampal input to it disrupts anxiety-related behavior and its representations of aversion (mouse).

entities.name: Prelimbic cortex
entities.summary: A medial prefrontal area of rodents. Its neurons show sustained responses during a 30 s conditioned tone that track freezing second by second, and their persistence after extinction training goes with failure to express extinction; inactivating it impairs fear expression but not extinction memory (rat). The authors of the recording study propose that it turns transient amygdala input into a sustained output that drives conditioned fear. Prelimbic lesions leave rats insensitive to changes in reward value even after limited training, suggesting it supports goal-directed action (rat). With competing shock- and sucrose-predictive cues, correlated firing between the basolateral amygdala and prelimbic cortex is directed mainly from the amygdala to prelimbic cortex during the shock cue, and stimulating this projection increases freezing (rat).

entities.name: Infralimbic cortex
entities.summary: A ventral medial prefrontal area of rodents. Its neurons fire to a conditioned tone when rats recall extinction the next day, with the largest increase in rats that freeze least, and pairing tones with brief infralimbic stimulation lowers freezing in rats that had not been extinguished. Inactivating it spares fear expression but impairs the acquisition and memory of extinction (rat). Infralimbic lesions keep rats sensitive to goal value even after extended training, suggesting that infralimbic cortex lets overtraining override goal-directed behavior (rat).

entities.name: Ventromedial prefrontal cortex
entities.summary: In humans, damage to it causes a defect in real-life decision-making: on a task that simulates such decisions, patients with prefrontal damage were oblivious to the future consequences of their actions. Patients with focal bilateral damage made abnormally utilitarian judgments on moral dilemmas that pit aggregate welfare against emotionally aversive actions, but not on other dilemmas. In healthy people, it encodes the values of specific options during comparative choice.

entities.name: Dorsal raphe nucleus
entities.summary: A serotonergic brainstem nucleus implicated in major depressive disorder. Selectively activating medial prefrontal neurons that project to it induced a profound, rapid and reversible effect on rats’ selection of an active response to a behavioral challenge.

entities.name: Working memory
entities.summary: Holding information for seconds to guide behavior. In monkeys, prefrontal neurons fire through memory delays with activity tuned to the remembered location, and blocking prefrontal D1 dopamine receptors impairs memory-guided, but not visually guided, saccades in a delay-dependent way. In mice, mediodorsal thalamic input to medial PFC supports maintenance and direct hippocampal input supports the encoding of spatial cues. Whether the memory is held by sustained firing or by brief oscillatory bursts is debated (monkey).

entities.name: Cognitive flexibility
entities.summary: Changing behavior when rules or outcomes change. In marmosets, lateral prefrontal damage impaired inhibitory control in attentional selection and orbitofrontal damage impaired it in affective processing; in rats, medial frontal lesions selectively impaired attentional set shifting. In monkeys, whether OFC is needed for reversal learning is debated: surgical removals impaired it, but excitotoxic, fiber-sparing lesions did not. In monkeys that flexibly select which sensory input guides a choice, selection and integration appear to unfold as one dynamical process within the same prefrontal circuits.

entities.name: Attention
entities.summary: Focusing processing on what matters for the task. In monkeys, prefrontal neurons signal the target location first during top-down attention, and parietal neurons first during bottom-up attention. In mice, mediodorsal thalamic input sustains prefrontal representations of the rules that guide attention. In ADHD, cortical maturation is delayed most prominently in prefrontal regions important for control of cognitive processes including attention (human).

entities.name: Value-based decision-making
entities.summary: Choosing among options by their value. In monkeys, orbitofrontal neurons encode the value of offered and chosen goods, and removing orbital prefrontal cortex blunts the change in choice that should follow a change in reward value. In humans, comparative and foraging modes of choice engage distinct mechanisms in ventromedial PFC and anterior cingulate cortex, and on a task that simulates real-life decisions, patients with ventromedial prefrontal damage seem guided by immediate prospects only, oblivious to future consequences.

entities.name: Fear learning & extinction
entities.summary: Learning that a cue predicts danger, and later that it no longer does (extinction), which is thought to form a new memory rather than erase the first. In rats, inactivating prelimbic cortex impairs the expression of conditioned fear, whereas inactivating infralimbic cortex spares it but impairs the acquisition and recall of extinction; inactivating the basolateral amygdala or ventral hippocampus impairs both. In mice, medial prefrontal theta input entrains the basolateral amygdala when animals recognize safety. Hippocampal lesions impair conditioning to the context but not to a tone, whereas amygdala lesions impair both (rat), and hippocampal lesions abolish contextual fear when made 1 day, but not 7 to 28 days, after training (rat). Optogenetically reactivating dentate gyrus cells tagged during fear conditioning is sufficient to induce freezing (mouse). Lesions of the lateral amygdala interfere with fear conditioning to a sound (rat), and pairing a tone with optogenetic activation of its pyramidal neurons makes the tone alone elicit fear (rat). The central amygdala is needed for acquiring as well as expressing conditioned fear (rat), and its CRF+ and SOM+ neurons compete to select flight or freezing (mouse). A patient with bilateral amygdala damage did not acquire conditioned autonomic responses but learned which stimuli were paired, whereas a patient with hippocampal damage showed the reverse (human).

entities.name: Goal-directed action & habits
entities.summary: Early in training, actions are goal-directed and sensitive to changes in the value of their outcome; extended training makes them habits that are not. In rats, prelimbic lesions abolish sensitivity to goal value even after limited training, whereas infralimbic lesions preserve it after extended training. In rats, lesions of the dorsolateral striatum, unlike dorsomedial lesions, kept lever pressing sensitive to outcome devaluation after training that generates habits, showing that the dorsolateral striatum is necessary for habit formation.

entities.name: Depression
entities.summary: In treatment-resistant depression, the subgenual cingulate (area 25) has been observed to be metabolically overactive, and chronic deep brain stimulation of the white matter next to it was associated with sustained remission in four of six patients (human). Ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist with rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant patients, rapidly builds spine synapses in rat prefrontal cortex through mTOR, and in mice it rescues spines lost on prefrontal projection neurons in depression-related states; these new spines are needed to maintain, but not to induce, its effects on motivated escape. Hippocampal volumes are smaller in people with a history of recurrent major depression, and the reduction correlates with its total duration (human); in mice, disrupting antidepressant-induced hippocampal neurogenesis blocks behavioral responses to antidepressants.

entities.name: ADHD
entities.summary: In 223 children with ADHD and 223 typically developing controls scanned repeatedly, the cortex reached peak thickness later in ADHD throughout most of the cerebrum (median 10.5 versus 7.5 years), most prominently in prefrontal regions important for control of cognitive processes including attention and motor planning; the regional order of maturation was similar in both groups (human).

entities.name: Ketamine
entities.summary: An NMDA receptor antagonist with rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression. In rats it rapidly activated mTOR signaling and increased the number and function of spine synapses in prefrontal cortex, and blocking mTOR prevented both this synaptogenesis and its behavioral effects in models of depression. In mice, antidepressant-dose ketamine rescued prefrontal spines eliminated in depression-related states, and this spinogenesis was needed to maintain, but not to induce, its effects on motivated escape. In monkey dorsolateral PFC, systemic ketamine abolished the persistent firing of Delay cells, while many Response cells fired more.

entities.name: Basal ganglia
entities.summary: Subcortical nuclei that control voluntary actions. Their major component, the striatum, sends two output systems, to the globus pallidus and to the substantia nigra, and is regulated in part by dopaminergic input from the substantia nigra. With the thalamus and cortex they form a basal ganglia–thalamocortical 'motor' circuit, and motor-related cortical areas also excite the pallidum through the subthalamic nucleus, bypassing the striatum (the 'hyperdirect' pathway). Specific disturbances of this circuit are postulated to account for hypokinetic disorders such as Parkinson's disease and for hyperkinetic ones such as Huntington's disease and hemiballismus.

entities.name: Globus pallidus, external segment (GPe)
entities.summary: Receives enkephalin-containing striatal projection neurons (human post-mortem tissue); in rats, these striatopallidal neurons also express D2 receptors. It is a station of the 'indirect' pathway from the striatum through the subthalamic nucleus to the internal pallidum. In Parkinsonian rats it has two GABAergic populations: prototypic neurons fire antiphase to the subthalamic nucleus, often express parvalbumin and target downstream nuclei including it, whereas arkypallidal neurons fire in phase with it, express preproenkephalin and innervate only the striatum, providing its largest extrinsic GABAergic input. In a Stop task, arkypallidal neurons respond to Stop cues earlier and more strongly than prototypical ones (rat).

entities.name: Globus pallidus, internal segment (GPi)
entities.summary: Receives substance P-containing striatal projection neurons (human post-mortem tissue) and is the last station of the 'indirect' pathway through the external pallidum and subthalamic nucleus; motor-related cortex also excites the globus pallidus through the subthalamic nucleus (the 'hyperdirect' pathway). In patients with Parkinson's disease off medication, its local potentials and their coherence with the subthalamic nucleus are dominated by activity below 30 Hz; levodopa reduces this activity and brings a new peak near 70 Hz.

entities.name: Substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr)
entities.summary: Receives substance P-containing striatal projection neurons (human post-mortem tissue); in rats, striatonigral neurons express D1 receptors and substance P. It exerts a tonic GABA-mediated inhibition on saccade-related cells of the superior colliculus: injecting the GABA agonist muscimol into it causes irrepressible saccades, most disrupting those to remembered targets, and the authors suggest that the basal ganglia contribute to initiating movement by releasing their target structures from tonic inhibition (monkey). In Huntington disease, substance P neurons projecting to it are more affected than those projecting to the pars compacta.

entities.name: Nucleus accumbens (ventral striatum)
entities.summary: The ventromedial, limbic part of the striatum, with a shell and a core. In monkeys it projects to a wide range of midbrain dopamine cells but receives a relatively small dopamine input; through these cells the shell influences the core, the core the central (associative) striatum and the central striatum the dorsolateral (motor) striatum, an ascending spiral that provides an anatomical basis for a limbic–cognitive–motor interface. In rats, goal-directed firing is most prominent in ventral CA1 neurons that target the nucleus accumbens. Mice work to earn optical stimulation of basolateral amygdala glutamatergic inputs to it, an effect that requires accumbal D1-type but not D2-type dopamine receptors.

entities.name: Direct-pathway neurons (D1)
entities.summary: Striatal projection neurons of the 'direct' pathway, classically proposed to facilitate movement. In rats, striatonigral neurons express D1 dopamine receptors and substance P, and dopamine loss lowers both mRNAs, which a D1 agonist reverses; in human tissue, substance P neurons project to the internal pallidum and the substantia nigra. In mice, optogenetically activating direct-pathway neurons reduced freezing and increased locomotion, and rescued freezing, bradykinesia and locomotor initiation in a Parkinson's disease model; yet they are transiently active together with indirect-pathway neurons when actions start, and both pathways are needed to initiate and execute learned action sequences. Dopamine acts on their cortical synapses in a way complementary to its action on D2 neurons (mouse).

entities.name: Indirect-pathway neurons (D2)
entities.summary: Striatal projection neurons that start the 'indirect' pathway, classically proposed to inhibit movement. In rats, striatopallidal neurons express D2 dopamine receptors and enkephalin, and dopamine loss raises both mRNAs, which a D2 agonist reverses; in human tissue, enkephalin-containing neurons project to the external pallidum. Bilaterally exciting them optogenetically produced a parkinsonian state with freezing, bradykinesia and fewer locomotor initiations (mouse), but they are also transiently active, with direct-pathway neurons, when mice initiate actions. In early and middle Huntington disease they are much more affected than substance P neurons projecting to the internal pallidum, and selective impairment of striatal neurons projecting to the lateral pallidum is postulated to cause hyperkinetic disorders.

entities.name: Corticostriatal plasticity
entities.summary: Long-term potentiation and depression at synapses from cortical pyramidal neurons onto striatal medium spiny neurons, forms of plasticity thought to underlie associative learning. Dopamine plays complementary roles in D1 and D2 neurons that keep this plasticity bidirectional and Hebbian, and in Parkinson's disease models the balance is lost, giving unidirectional changes (mouse slices). Stimulating the substantia nigra with the parameters optimal for self-stimulation potentiated corticostriatal synapses through dopamine receptors, and the potentiation correlated with the time rats took to learn the task; the authors propose that this potentiation reinforces the learned behaviour (rat).

entities.name: Reward prediction error (dopamine)
entities.summary: A discrepancy between actual and expected outcomes, proposed to support learning about the cues that predict reward. The fluctuating output of primate dopamine neurons apparently signals errors in the predictions of future rewarding events, in line with quantitative theories of adaptive optimizing control. Optogenetically activating dopamine neurons at reward delivery, mimicking a prediction error, was sufficient for long-lasting increases in cue-elicited reward seeking (rat). In mice, dopaminergic axons that signal locomotion were largely distinct from those responding to unexpected rewards, and SNc neurons active before movement did not overlap with reward-responsive ones.

entities.name: Low-frequency STN–pallidal synchrony
entities.summary: In local potentials recorded after surgery in patients with Parkinson's disease, power within and coherence between the subthalamic nucleus and internal pallidum are dominated off medication by activity below 30 Hz; levodopa reduces it and brings a new peak near 70 Hz, so the pattern of synchronization depends critically on dopaminergic activity (four patients).

entities.name: Alpha-synuclein (SNCA)
entities.summary: A presynaptic protein thought to be involved in neuronal plasticity. A mutation in its gene was identified in an Italian kindred and three unrelated Greek families with autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease, and it forms the major filamentous component of Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, the defining lesions of Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.

entities.name: IT15 (huntingtin) gene
entities.summary: The Huntington's disease gene on 4p16.3, isolated with the help of haplotype analysis of linkage disequilibrium. It contains a polymorphic (CAG)n trinucleotide repeat, apparently within the coding sequence of a widely expressed protein of about 348 kd unrelated to any known gene; the repeat is expanded and unstable on disease chromosomes, like the unstable DNA segments described in fragile X syndrome, spino-bulbar muscular atrophy and myotonic dystrophy.

entities.name: Levodopa
entities.summary: The dopamine precursor, given to reduce the symptoms of Parkinson's disease. In a 40-week placebo-controlled trial in early disease, parkinsonism worsened less at every levodopa dose, even after 2 weeks off treatment, but striatal dopamine-transporter uptake declined more; whether levodopa slows the disease or has a prolonged effect on symptoms remains uncertain, and the highest dose caused more dyskinesia. In many patients, treatment is complicated by fluctuations between 'off' periods and 'on' periods often accompanied by debilitating dyskinesias. In patients' subthalamic nucleus and internal pallidum, it reduces activity below 30 Hz and brings a new peak near 70 Hz.

entities.name: Deep brain stimulation (STN or pallidum)
entities.summary: An accepted treatment for advanced Parkinson disease. After a year of bilateral subthalamic stimulation, off-medication daily-living and motor scores improved by 60 percent and the dopaminergic dose was halved (24 patients), and in randomized trials subthalamic or pallidal stimulation beat best medical therapy on motor function and quality of life in advanced disease, as subthalamic stimulation did in patients with early motor complications, at the cost of more serious adverse events. In parkinsonian rodents, its therapeutic effects within the subthalamic nucleus can be accounted for by selective stimulation of afferent axons projecting there. Stimulating only when local field potentials from the electrodes showed pathological activity (adaptive DBS) improved motor scores more than continuous stimulation, with 56 percent less stimulation time (8 patients).

entities.name: Parkinson's disease
entities.summary: A common neurodegenerative disorder, with a lifetime incidence of about 2 percent, that results from a loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra; this loss causes deficits in movement initiation and slowness of movement. Its defining lesions, Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, are made mainly of alpha-synuclein filaments, and a mutation in the alpha-synuclein gene was found in families with autosomal dominant disease. MPTP, a product of meperidine-analog synthesis found in an illicit drug, causes chronic parkinsonism in humans and is proposed to damage substantia nigra cells selectively. Levodopa reduces symptoms, and subthalamic or pallidal stimulation improves motor function and quality of life in advanced disease, as subthalamic stimulation does in patients with early motor complications.

entities.name: Huntington's disease
entities.summary: A dominantly inherited hyperkinetic movement disorder. Its mutation involves an unstable DNA segment: a (CAG)n repeat in the IT15 gene on 4p16.3 that is longer than normal on disease chromosomes from all 75 families examined. It is characterized by the loss of striatal projection neurons; in early and middle stages, enkephalin-containing neurons projecting to the external pallidum are much more affected than substance P neurons projecting to the internal pallidum. Hyperkinetic disorders are postulated to result from selective impairment of striatal neurons projecting to the lateral pallidum.

entities.name: Movement vigor
entities.summary: The speed or amplitude of movement. Dopaminergic input to the dorsal striatum is indispensable for the striatal activity that mediates adaptive changes in vigor: progressive dopamine depletion reduced vigor and its striatal representation, restoring dopaminergic tone ameliorated both, and suppressing striatal activity during movement reduced vigor (mouse). Activity of SNc dopamine neurons before self-paced movement is related to the vigour of the coming movement, and inhibiting or activating them while mice are immobile lowers or raises it.

entities.name: Action sequences
entities.summary: Learning, starting and stopping ordered series of actions, whose initiation and termination are compromised in Parkinson's and Huntington's diseases. As mice learn a sequence, activity in nigrostriatal circuits comes to signal its start and stop, and genetically altering striatal circuits disrupts this activity and sequence learning. Both the direct and the indirect striatal pathways are needed to initiate and execute learned sequences (mouse).

entities.name: Superior colliculus
entities.summary: Midbrain structure whose saccade-related cells are under tonic GABA-mediated inhibition, a substantial fraction of it from the substantia nigra pars reticulata: muscimol injected into the pars reticulata has the same general effect as the GABA antagonist bicuculline injected into the colliculus, irrepressible saccades (monkey).

entities.name: Entorhinal cortex
entities.summary: The gateway connecting the neocortex and the hippocampal formation. Its layer II gives rise to the perforant pathway, the major source of excitatory input to the hippocampus, and its layer IV receives a major hippocampal efferent projection. The dorsocaudal medial entorhinal cortex contains grid cells (rat). In Alzheimer's disease, neurofibrillary changes affect the transentorhinal region first and then the entorhinal cortex proper, and layer II neurons are already 60% fewer in very mild disease (human).

entities.name: Dentate gyrus
entities.summary: Receives the perforant path from the entorhinal cortex and projects to CA3: the first two steps of the trisynaptic pathway. Conditioning trains to the perforant path potentiate its granule-cell responses for up to 10 hours (rabbit). Models have long pointed to it as a possible source of pattern separation: small changes to an environment change granule-cell activity patterns (rat), deleting granule-cell NMDA receptors impairs telling similar contexts apart (mouse), and human CA3/dentate gyrus activity is biased toward pattern separation. New neurons continue to be generated in its subgranular zone in adult mammals; whether this persists in adult humans is debated. Dorsal granule cells control exploratory drive and the encoding of contextual fear memories, and raising ventral granule-cell activity suppresses innate anxiety (mouse).

entities.name: CA3
entities.summary: Receives dentate gyrus input and projects to CA1. Its extensive recurrent connectivity has led to suggestions that it might complete memories from partial cues: mice lacking CA3 NMDA receptors acquire and retrieve a water-maze memory normally but are impaired when only a fraction of the original cues remains. Its recurrent excitation also generates the sharp waves that drive ripples in CA1 (review). When environments are made more different, CA3 recruits new cell populations (rat).

entities.name: CA2
entities.summary: A relatively small area between CA3 and CA1 that forms the nexus of a powerful disynaptic circuit linking entorhinal input with CA1 output. Genetically inactivating CA2 pyramidal neurons causes a pronounced loss of social memory, with no change in sociability or in spatial and contextual memory (mouse).

entities.name: CA1
entities.summary: The main hippocampal output and the last step of the trisynaptic pathway, with input from CA3 and, through a disynaptic circuit, CA2. A bilateral lesion limited to CA1 caused enduring anterograde amnesia (human); deleting NMDA receptors from CA1 pyramidal cells abolishes LTP there and impairs spatial memory (mouse); and one-trial inhibitory avoidance learning induces LTP in CA1 (rat). Ripples arise in CA1 from CA3 sharp waves (review). Dorsal CA1 is enriched in place cells and ventral CA1 in anxiety cells (mouse).

entities.name: Subiculum
entities.summary: Part of the hippocampal formation. In Alzheimer's disease, pathology specifically affects cells of the subiculum and of entorhinal layers II and IV, the cells that interconnect the hippocampal formation with the association cortices, basal forebrain, thalamus and hypothalamus (human). In high-resolution fMRI its activity, like that of CA1 and the entorhinal cortex, was biased toward pattern completion (human).

entities.name: Dorsal (posterior) hippocampus
entities.summary: The dorsal hippocampus of rodents, which corresponds to the posterior hippocampus in primates, performs primarily cognitive functions (review). Posterior hippocampi are larger in licensed London taxi drivers than in controls, and their volume correlates with time spent as a taxi driver (human); dorsal CA1 is enriched in place cells (mouse); and dorsal dentate granule cells control exploratory drive and the encoding, not retrieval, of contextual fear memories (mouse). The view of a sharp dorsal–ventral dichotomy may need revision (review).

entities.name: Ventral (anterior) hippocampus
entities.summary: The ventral hippocampus of rodents, which corresponds to the anterior hippocampus in primates, relates to stress, emotion and affect, and its gene expression correlates with that of the amygdala and hypothalamus (review). Raising ventral dentate granule-cell activity powerfully suppresses innate anxiety (mouse), and ventral CA1 is enriched in anxiety cells, especially among neurons projecting to the lateral hypothalamic area (mouse). Ventral CA1 neurons route different information to different targets: anxiety-related firing to the prefrontal cortex and goal-directed firing to the nucleus accumbens (rat). Basolateral amygdala inputs to it are monosynaptic and glutamatergic onto pyramidal neurons, and activating them increases anxiety-related behavior (mouse).

entities.name: Medial septum
entities.summary: Inactivating the medial septum, with muscimol or intraseptal lidocaine, reduces theta oscillations, and entorhinal grid cells then lose their spatial periodicity while head-direction cells keep their selectivity (rat).

entities.name: Place cells
entities.summary: Hippocampal neurons whose primary correlate is the animal's location in an environment (rat); unit activity in freely moving rats gave preliminary evidence that the hippocampus acts as a spatial map. Cells that respond at specific locations in a virtual town are found mainly in the human hippocampus. As a rat crosses a place field, the theta phase of firing moves progressively forward on each cycle (phase precession). Cells active together during behavior fire together more in later slow-wave sleep, and before goal-directed navigation place-cell sequences depict paths to a remembered goal (rat). Most place cells 'remap' when a salient spatial cue is altered.

entities.name: Grid cells
entities.summary: Neurons of the medial entorhinal cortex that fire whenever the animal's position coincides with a vertex of a regular triangular grid spanning the environment; grid spacing increases from dorsal to ventral, and the map is anchored to landmarks but persists without them, suggesting a path-integration-based map (rat). Layer II is predominated by grid cells, while deeper layers add head-direction and conjunctive grid × head-direction cells, all modulated by running speed (rat). Grid periodicity vanishes when medial septal inactivation reduces theta (rat). Cells with grid-like spiking have been recorded in neurosurgical patients performing a virtual-navigation task (human).

entities.name: Time cells
entities.summary: Hippocampal neurons that encode successive moments during an empty gap between key events, while also encoding location and ongoing behavior; most form a different representation ('retime') when the main temporal parameter is altered (rat).

entities.name: Memory engram cells
entities.summary: A specific memory is thought to be encoded by a sparse population of neurons, which can be tagged during learning. Optogenetically reactivating dentate gyrus neurons tagged during fear conditioning induces freezing in another context, and reactivating cells tagged in one context while the mouse is fear-conditioned in another creates a false fear memory (mouse). For remote memory, prefrontal engram cells are generated during learning through hippocampal–entorhinal and basolateral amygdala inputs and mature with time, while hippocampal engram cells gradually become silent (mouse).

entities.name: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis
entities.summary: New neurons continue to be generated in the subgranular zone of the dentate gyrus in adult mammals. In mice, ablating adult neurogenesis impairs discrimination between nearby locations, increasing the survival of adult-born neurons improves discrimination between similar contexts, and disrupting antidepressant-induced neurogenesis blocks behavioral responses to antidepressants. Whether it continues in adult humans is debated: new neurons were found in the dentate gyrus of adult patients labelled with BrdU (human), young neurons were not detected in adults in one study (human; in macaques neurogenesis declined during juvenile development), and thousands of immature neurons were counted at ages 14 to 79 in another (human).

entities.name: Hippocampal LTP
entities.summary: Long-term potentiation of hippocampal synapses. Conditioning trains to the perforant path potentiate dentate granule-cell responses for up to 10 hours (rabbit). Blocking NMDA receptors with AP5 suppresses it in vivo and impairs place learning (rat), deleting NMDA receptors from CA1 pyramidal cells abolishes CA1 LTP and impairs spatial memory (mouse), and one-trial inhibitory avoidance learning itself induces LTP in CA1 (rat).

entities.name: NMDA receptors (hippocampus)
entities.summary: Glutamate receptors activated by NMDA that become active only on depolarization; blocking them with AP5 does not detectably affect hippocampal synaptic transmission but prevents the induction of LTP, and chronic AP5 impairs place learning (rat). Deleting them in one subregion at a time shows distinct roles: in CA1 pyramidal cells for LTP and spatial memory, in CA3 pyramidal cells for recall from partial cues, and in dentate granule cells for distinguishing similar contexts (mouse).

entities.name: Sharp-wave ripples & replay
entities.summary: The most synchronous population pattern in the mammalian brain, occurring in 'off-line' states such as non-REM sleep: they arise from the excitatory recurrent system of CA3, drive a fast ripple oscillation in CA1 and replay fragments of waking sequences in compressed form (review). Place cells that fired together during behavior fire together more in later slow-wave sleep (rat). Selectively suppressing ripples after training impairs spatial memory, and disrupting ripple-associated activity during rest slows learning (rat). Their pathological conversion ('p-ripples') is a marker of epileptogenic tissue (review).

entities.name: Theta rhythm
entities.summary: A rhythm of the hippocampal EEG (7–12 Hz; 4–11 Hz in a study of entorhinal grid cells) that is better correlated with movements that change the rat's location; place cells fire at a theta phase that moves progressively forward as the rat crosses a field (rat). Reducing theta by inactivating the medial septum abolishes the spatial periodicity of entorhinal grid cells but spares head-direction tuning (rat).

entities.name: Pattern separation
entities.summary: Transforming similar representations or memories into highly dissimilar, nonoverlapping ones, a key component of many functions ascribed to the hippocampus. Evidence points to the dentate gyrus and CA3: dentate activity patterns change with minimal changes to an environment (rat), deleting dentate NMDA receptors impairs telling similar contexts apart (mouse), ablating adult neurogenesis impairs fine spatial discrimination and increasing it improves context discrimination (mouse), and human CA3/dentate gyrus activity is biased toward pattern separation.

entities.name: Pattern completion
entities.summary: Retrieving complete memories from incomplete sets of cues. The extensive recurrent connectivity of CA3 suggested that it might provide this function, and mice lacking CA3 NMDA receptors are impaired at recall from partial cues (mouse). In human fMRI, activity biased toward pattern completion was seen in CA1, the subiculum and the entorhinal and parahippocampal cortices (human).

entities.name: Episodic & declarative memory
entities.summary: Long-term memory for facts and events. Its establishment depends on a medial temporal lobe system of the hippocampus and adjacent cortex (review). Loss of recent memory follows bilateral hippocampal lesions, a lesion limited to CA1 caused enduring anterograde amnesia, and patients with hippocampal amnesia are markedly impaired at imagining new experiences, which lack spatial coherence (human). Hippocampal time cells bridge temporal gaps between discontiguous events (rat).

entities.name: Memory consolidation
entities.summary: How new memories become enduring. Memories of everyday life depend initially on the medial temporal lobe and are thought to come to rely on cortex as they mature (review), and hippocampal lesions abolish contextual fear when made 1 day, but not 7 to 28 days, after conditioning (rat). Systems consolidation can occur very quickly when a neocortical schema exists (rat). Sharp wave-ripples are believed to transfer labile memories to the neocortex, and suppressing them after training impairs spatial memory (rat). Prefrontal engram cells for remote fear memory form during learning and mature over time, while hippocampal engram cells gradually become silent (mouse). The basolateral amygdala mediates the memory-modulating effects of adrenal stress hormones and modulates the consolidation of many kinds of memory (review). A consolidated fear memory that is reactivated returns to a labile state: blocking protein synthesis in the lateral and basal amygdala shortly after reactivation produces amnesia (rat).

entities.name: Anxiety
entities.summary: Innate anxiety and the avoidance of anxiogenic places. Raising ventral dentate granule-cell activity powerfully suppresses innate anxiety (mouse); ventral CA1 anxiety cells, activated by anxiogenic environments, are required for avoidance, and activating their terminals in the lateral hypothalamus increases anxiety and avoidance (mouse); and inhibiting ventral hippocampal input to the medial prefrontal cortex disrupts anxiety-related behavior (mouse). Stimulating basolateral amygdala terminals in the central amygdala reduces anxiety-related behavior, and inhibiting them increases it, whereas activating basolateral amygdala synapses in the ventral hippocampus increases anxiety-related behavior (mouse). Bilateral central amygdala lesions reduce fear-related behavior toward a snake and freezing toward a human intruder and lower cerebrospinal fluid CRF and plasma ACTH, which suggests that the central amygdala plays a role in fear- and anxiety-related behavioral and endocrine responses (monkey).

entities.name: Social memory
entities.summary: The ability of an animal to remember a conspecific. Genetically inactivating CA2 pyramidal neurons causes a pronounced loss of social memory without changing sociability (mouse).

entities.name: Amnesia
entities.summary: Studies of human amnesia, and of a monkey model of it, identified the medial temporal lobe memory system (review). Loss of recent memory follows bilateral hippocampal lesions; a lesion limited to CA1 caused marked anterograde amnesia with little if any retrograde amnesia; and amnesic patients with primary bilateral hippocampal damage are markedly impaired at imagining new experiences (human).

entities.name: Alzheimer's disease
entities.summary: Neurofibrillary tangles and neuropil threads follow a characteristic distribution that defines six stages: transentorhinal (I–II), limbic (III–IV, with the entorhinal cortex proper and mild involvement of the first Ammon's horn sector) and isocortical (V–VI); amyloid deposits are of limited use for staging (human). Pathology of the subiculum and of entorhinal layers II and IV isolates the hippocampal formation from much of its input and output and probably contributes to the memory disorder, and layer II entorhinal neurons are already 60% fewer in very mild disease (human).

entities.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
entities.summary: In monozygotic twins discordant for trauma exposure, PTSD severity correlated negatively with the hippocampal volume of both the exposed patients and their unexposed co-twins, evidence that smaller hippocampi are a risk factor for stress-related psychopathology (human). Veterans with PTSD show exaggerated amygdala responses to masked fearful versus happy faces compared with combat-exposed veterans without PTSD (human). A meta-analysis found greater amygdala and insula activity in PTSD, social anxiety disorder and specific phobia, and hypoactivation of the dorsal and rostral anterior cingulate and ventromedial prefrontal cortex only in PTSD (human).

entities.name: Antidepressants
entities.summary: Chronic antidepressant treatments increase adult hippocampal neurogenesis. Serotonin 1A receptor null mice are insensitive to the neurogenic and behavioral effects of fluoxetine, a serotonin selective reuptake inhibitor, and X-irradiating a region containing the hippocampus prevents the effects of two classes of antidepressants (mouse).

entities.name: Lateral amygdala
entities.summary: A major subcortical target of the auditory thalamus. Lesions of it, but not of the striatum above it or the adjacent cortex, interfere with fear conditioning to a sound, so it may be the sensory interface of the amygdala in emotional learning (rat). Fear conditioning increases the tone-evoked responses of its neurons, often within the first few trials (rat), potentiates its input from the medial geniculate nucleus (rat), and drives AMPA receptors into the synapses of a large fraction of its neurons; blocking that delivery in as few as 10 to 20% of them reduces the memory (rat). Pairing a tone with optogenetic activation of its pyramidal neurons, in place of a shock, makes the tone alone elicit fear (rat). Changing CREB function in subsets of its neurons changes the probability that they are recruited into a fear memory trace, and deleting the neurons that overexpressed CREB after learning blocks expression of the memory (mouse).

entities.name: Basolateral amygdala
entities.summary: Here the basal nuclei (basolateral and basomedial); the lateral nucleus is shown separately. Switches between high fear (renewal) and low fear (extinction) are triggered by a rapid change in the balance of activity between two populations of basal amygdala neurons, differentially connected with the hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex (mouse). Its neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens or to the centromedial amygdala undergo opposing synaptic changes after reward or fear conditioning (mouse), and two genetically distinct populations take part in positive- and negative-valence behaviors and inhibit each other (mouse). Stimulating its terminals in the central amygdala reduces anxiety-related behavior, whereas activating its synapses in the ventral hippocampus increases it (mouse). Animal studies indicate that the basolateral complex mediates the memory-modulating effects of adrenal stress hormones and modulates the consolidation of many kinds of memory (review).

entities.name: Central amygdala
entities.summary: The principal output nucleus for the expression of conditioned fear responses. Different efferent projections appear to mediate the behavioral and autonomic parts of conditioned fear: lesions of the lateral hypothalamic area, one of its targets, interfere with the conditioned arterial pressure response but not freezing, whereas lesions of the caudal midbrain central gray disrupt freezing but not the pressure response (rat). It is needed for the acquisition as well as the expression of fear conditioning, and blocking protein synthesis in it after training impairs consolidation (rat). Activity in its lateral subdivision (CEl) is required for fear acquisition, whereas output neurons of its medial subdivision (CEm) drive conditioned fear responses (mouse), and an inhibitory pathway from it to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray produces freezing (mouse). Its projections to nuclei that modulate freezing or cardiovascular responses arise from separate populations that respond differently to oxytocin (rat). In monkeys, bilateral lesions reduce fear-related behavior toward a snake and freezing toward a human intruder and lower cerebrospinal fluid CRF.

entities.name: Intercalated cells
entities.summary: Clusters of neurons that receive information about the conditioned stimulus from the basolateral amygdala and send inhibitory projections to the central nucleus. After extinction training they could reduce the impact of basolateral input on the central nucleus by feed-forward inhibition. Partially lesioning them, with a toxin that targets cells expressing μ-opioid receptors, causes a marked deficit in the expression of fear extinction, larger the fewer intercalated neurons survive (rat).

entities.name: Medial amygdala
entities.summary: Implicated in prototypic social behaviors such as aggression. A GABAergic subpopulation promotes aggression and two other social behaviors and inhibits self-grooming, whereas neighboring glutamatergic neurons promote repetitive self-grooming and inhibit social interactions, so inhibitory and excitatory subpopulations control social and repetitive asocial behaviors antagonistically (mouse).

entities.name: CEl PKC-δ+ neurons
entities.summary: GABAergic neurons of the lateral central amygdala that inhibit output neurons of the medial central amygdala and make reciprocal inhibitory synapses with PKC-δ− neurons. Silencing them suggests that they are the CEl 'off' units, inhibited by the conditioned stimulus, of an inhibitory microcircuit that gates central amygdala output to control conditioned freezing (mouse). They are also activated by diverse anorexigenic signals, are required for those signals to inhibit feeding, and strongly suppress food intake when activated (mouse).

entities.name: CEl SOM+ neurons
entities.summary: Somatostatin-positive inhibitory neurons of the lateral central amygdala. Preventing fear-conditioning-induced synaptic potentiation onto them impairs fear memory formation, and activating them is necessary for fear memory recall and sufficient to drive fear responses; the authors propose that they inhibit CEl output, disinhibiting the medial central amygdala and releasing fear expression (mouse). In mice that switch between conditioned freezing and flight, activating SOM+ central amygdala neurons initiates freezing.

entities.name: CeA CRF+ neurons
entities.summary: In mice that switch between conditioned freezing and flight, CRF+ central amygdala neurons mediate conditioned flight, whereas SOM+ neurons initiate freezing; local inhibitory connections between the two populations regulate the balance, so competition between them selects the response (mouse).

entities.name: Synaptic plasticity in fear learning
entities.summary: Fear conditioning itself produces a long-lasting increase in synaptic efficacy in the pathway from the medial geniculate nucleus to the lateral amygdala, measured in vitro as a presynaptic facilitation of AMPA-receptor-mediated transmission (rat), and drives AMPA receptors into the synapses of a large fraction of lateral amygdala neurons (rat). After rats learn to associate a foot shock with optogenetic stimulation of auditory inputs to the amygdala, optogenetic long-term depression of those inputs inactivates the memory and later long-term potentiation reactivates it, supporting a causal link between these synaptic processes and memory (rat).

entities.name: CREB and memory allocation
entities.summary: Changing CREB function in subsets of lateral amygdala neurons changes the probability that individual neurons are recruited into a fear memory trace, suggesting that eligible neurons compete and are selected according to their relative CREB activity at the time of learning (mouse). Selectively deleting the neurons that overexpressed CREB after learning, but not a similar proportion of random lateral amygdala neurons, blocks expression of that memory robustly and persistently (mouse).

entities.name: Medial geniculate nucleus (auditory thalamus)
entities.summary: Part of the auditory (acoustic) thalamus. Its medial division, with the posterior intralaminar and suprageniculate nuclei, projects to the amygdala. Destroying either the thalamo-amygdala or the thalamo-cortico-amygdala auditory pathway alone leaves auditory fear conditioning intact, whereas destroying both disrupts it (rat). Fear conditioning produces a long-lasting increase in synaptic efficacy in its pathway to the lateral amygdala (rat).

entities.name: Emotional valence
entities.summary: Whether a stimulus or outcome is good or bad. Amygdala neurons encode the positive and negative values of images, and distinct populations encode each (monkey). In mice, basolateral amygdala neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens support positive reinforcement and those projecting to the centromedial amygdala negative reinforcement, and two genetically distinct basolateral populations take part in positive- and negative-valence behaviors. Two people with focal bilateral amygdala lesions showed a dramatic reduction in loss aversion in monetary gambles (human).

entities.name: Anxiety disorders
entities.summary: A meta-analysis of imaging studies found that patients with social anxiety disorder, specific phobia or PTSD consistently show greater activity than comparison subjects in the amygdala and insula, structures linked to negative emotional responses, as do healthy subjects during fear conditioning (human).

their axons form the corticospinal tract
descending excitation from the upper layers drives layer 5 output neurons (corticospinal neurons in upper L5B)

new spines formed and stabilized during training are associated with durable skill memory (mouse)

D1/D2 receptor blockade in M1 reduces LTP and impairs skill acquisition (rat)

competing accounts: tuning to movement parameters versus population dynamics

Chx10+ interneurons needed for skilled reaching, Vglut3+ for releasing food (mouse)

Pten deletion (raising mTOR activity) lets injured corticospinal axons regenerate (mouse)

links.rel: D1-receptor actions on delay firing are mediated by cAMP signaling (monkeys and rats)

Delay-cell persistent firing in dorsolateral PFC needs NR2B-containing NMDA receptors (monkey)
systemic ketamine abolished Delay-cell persistent firing in dorsolateral PFC, while many Response cells fired more (monkey)

recurrent excitation among pyramidal Delay cells generates persistent firing (monkey)
dendritic spine density on deep layer 3 pyramidal neurons of DLPFC area 46 is 23% lower in schizophrenia than in controls (human)
depression-related behavior goes with branch-specific spine loss on prefrontal projection neurons (mouse)
excitatory synaptic strength onto layer V mPFC pyramidal neurons tracks dominance rank, and raising or lowering synaptic efficacy in dorsal mPFC moves rank up or down (mouse)
inhibiting parvalbumin interneurons suppresses gamma oscillations, and driving them is sufficient to generate gamma rhythmicity (mouse neocortex)
links.note: Review (lewis2005): in schizophrenia, reduced GABA synthesis in DLPFC parvalbumin interneurons alters perisomatic inhibition of pyramidal neurons, which contributes to a diminished capacity for gamma-frequency synchrony.

links.rel: convergent findings: in schizophrenia, deficient TrkB signaling reduces GABA synthesis in DLPFC parvalbumin interneurons (review)
inhibiting mPFC somatostatin (not parvalbumin) interneurons during encoding impairs spatial working memory (mouse)

persistent delay firing as the store of working memory

links.rel: gamma bursts accompany encoding and re-activation (monkey); hippocampal-prefrontal gamma synchrony appears to mediate cue encoding (mouse); hippocampal-prefrontal theta coupling strengthens during spatial working memory (rat)
mixed-selectivity neurons carry information about all task-relevant aspects, and the dimensionality of this representation collapses on error trials (monkey)

single-neuron responses make sense as population dynamics that a trained recurrent network reproduces; the authors propose that context-dependent selection and integration of inputs are one dynamical process (monkey)
prefrontal neurons code abstract rules (monkey); theory casts prefrontal representations of goals and the means to achieve them as bias signals to other brain structures
mediodorsal input amplifies local prefrontal connectivity to sustain rule representations, without relaying categorical information (mouse)
the parvicellular mediodorsal nucleus connects with dorsolateral areas 46 and 9 (monkey)
the magnocellular mediodorsal nucleus connects with orbital and medial areas 11–14 (monkey)
mediodorsal input sustains mPFC delay activity during working memory and prefrontal rule representations during attention (mouse)
the mPFC-to-mediodorsal projection supports the choice that follows the delay (mouse)
direct hippocampal input supports the encoding of spatial cues in working memory (mouse); CA1-mPFC firing correlations and theta coupling strengthen during spatial working memory (rat)
hippocampal-formation neurons project mostly to medial, then orbital, prefrontal areas and only sparsely to lateral areas (monkey)
dense connections with posterior orbitofrontal cortex, whose caudal areas receive more amygdala input than they send (monkey)
cingulate area 24 sends comparatively more projections to the amygdala than it receives (monkey)
subgenual area 25 sends comparatively more projections to the amygdala than it receives (monkey)
basolateral amygdala firing entrains to mPFC theta input when mice recognize safety
proposed: prelimbic cortex turns transient amygdala input into a sustained output that drives conditioned fear (rat)
selectively activating mPFC neurons that project to the dorsal raphe had a profound, rapid and reversible effect on the selection of active behavior in a challenging situation (rat)
links.note: Activating mPFC principal neurons without regard to their projection had no detectable effect.

links.rel: dopaminergic projection from a distinct fast-firing population (mouse); phasic release in mPFC tunes its neurons to relevant cues during learning (mouse)
noradrenergic projection; LC cells projecting to PFC differ from those projecting to motor cortex and release more noradrenaline (rat)
frontal-parietal synchrony is stronger at lower frequencies during top-down and at higher frequencies during bottom-up attention (monkey)
prelimbic activity tracks freezing, and inactivating prelimbic cortex impairs the expression of conditioned fear (rat)
infralimbic activity signals extinction recall, stimulating it mimics extinction, and inactivating it impairs extinction learning and memory (rat)

an important component of the system for acquiring, storing and expressing fear memory (review); amygdala lesions interfere with fear conditioning to a tone and to the context, and inactivating the basolateral amygdala impairs fear expression and extinction memory (rat); a patient with bilateral amygdala damage did not acquire conditioned autonomic responses, and unilateral temporal lobectomy impairs fear conditioning (human)

hippocampal lesions impair fear conditioning to the context but not to a tone, and abolish contextual fear when made 1 day, but not 7 to 28 days, after training; inactivating the ventral hippocampus impairs fear expression and extinction memory (rat)
prelimbic lesions abolish sensitivity to goal value (rat)
infralimbic lesions keep actions goal-directed after extended training (rat)
medial frontal lesions selectively impair attentional set shifting (rat)
inhibiting mPFC somatostatin interneurons or hippocampal input during cue encoding, or mediodorsal input during maintenance, impairs spatial working memory (mouse)
its neurons hold directionally tuned delay activity for remembered locations, which depends on NR2B NMDA receptors (monkey)
lateral prefrontal (area 9) damage causes a loss of inhibitory control in attentional selection (marmoset)
DLPFC blood flow fails to rise during the Wisconsin Card Sort in patients and tracks their performance (human)
OFC neurons encode the value of offered and chosen goods, independent of spatial and motor factors (monkey)
value signals for the options under choice: in OFC neurons (monkey) and vmPFC activity (human)
orbital prefrontal removals attenuate the effect of reinforcer devaluation on choices, and fiber-sparing lesion results favor a role in value updating (monkey)
links.note: Theory (wilson2014) proposes that OFC labels the current task state for reinforcement learning elsewhere in the brain.

links.rel: needed for reversal learning? results depend on the lesion method (monkey; marmoset)
links.note: Surgical removals of orbital prefrontal cortex impaired object reversal learning (izquierdo2004, monkey), and OFC damage impaired inhibitory control in affective processing (dias1996, marmoset), but excitotoxic, fiber-sparing OFC lesions spared reversal learning, and a previously reported loss of inhibitory control was traced to damage to nearby fiber tracts (rudebeck2013, monkey).

links.rel: damage leaves patients oblivious to future consequences, and its activity encodes the values of specific options (human)
bilateral damage makes judgments on emotionally aversive moral dilemmas abnormally utilitarian (human)
conflict-related activity predicts prefrontal activity and behavioral adjustments (human); theory proposes that dorsal ACC allocates control according to its expected value
encodes the average value of the foraging environment and the cost of foraging (human)
reported to be metabolically overactive in treatment-resistant depression; chronic stimulation of the adjacent white matter was associated with sustained remission in four of six patients (human)
cortical maturation is delayed in ADHD, most prominently in prefrontal regions (human)
prefrontal neurons signal the attended location first during top-down attention (monkey), and mediodorsal-sustained prefrontal rule representations guide attention (mouse)
striatonigral projection: substance P neurons (human), which in rats also express D1 receptors
substance P-containing striatal neurons project to the internal pallidum: the 'direct' pathway
striatopallidal projection: enkephalin-containing neurons (human), which in rats also express D2 receptors
prototypic pallidal neurons, often parvalbumin-positive, target the subthalamic nucleus (rat): the 'indirect' pathway
arkypallidal neurons innervate only the striatum, its largest extrinsic GABAergic input, and respond to Stop cues (rat)
excitatory relay of the 'hyperdirect' and 'indirect' pathways to the pallidum
links.note: In patients with Parkinson's disease off medication, local potentials in the two nuclei are dominated by coherent activity below 30 Hz, which levodopa reduces (brown2001).

links.rel: 'hyperdirect' pathway: motor-related cortical areas excite the subthalamic nucleus, bypassing the striatum, with a shorter conduction time than paths through it
pallidal output to the thalamus closes the basal ganglia–thalamocortical 'motor' circuit
tonic GABA-mediated inhibition of saccade-related collicular cells; muscimol in the pars reticulata releases irrepressible saccades (monkey)
the ventromedial (limbic) striatum projects to a wide range of midbrain dopamine cells, part of an ascending striatonigrostriatal spiral (monkey)
acts on striatonigral neurons through D1 receptors: dopamine loss lowers their D1-receptor and substance P mRNAs, which a D1 agonist reverses (rat)
acts on striatopallidal neurons through D2 receptors: dopamine loss raises their D2-receptor and enkephalin mRNAs, which a D2 agonist reverses (rat)
complementary actions in D1 and D2 neurons keep corticostriatal plasticity bidirectional and Hebbian; unidirectional in Parkinson's disease models (mouse)
nigral stimulation at self-stimulation parameters potentiates corticostriatal synapses through dopamine receptors (rat)
proposed to reinforce learned actions: the potentiation correlated with the time rats took to learn self-stimulation (rat)
the fluctuating output of dopamine neurons apparently signals reward prediction errors (primate)
activating dopamine neurons at reward delivery, mimicking a prediction error, is sufficient for long-lasting increases in cue-elicited reward seeking (rat)
activating direct-pathway neurons reduces freezing and increases locomotion, and rescues locomotor initiation in a Parkinson's disease model (mouse)
links.note: Both pathways are transiently active when actions start (cui2013), and manipulating striatonigral neurons before a learned sequence slows its initiation (tecuapetla2016).

links.rel: classically inhibits movement: bilateral activation produces freezing and fewer locomotor initiations (mouse); yet indirect-pathway neurons are also active when actions start
links.note: kravitz2010 supports the classical opposing model. cui2013 found direct- and indirect-pathway neurons concurrently active at action initiation, and tecuapetla2016 found both pathways necessary for initiating and executing learned sequences (manipulating the striatopallidal pathway before initiation aborted it), and suggests a supportive versus permissive model rather than opposition.

links.rel: inhibiting dopamine neurons while mice are immobile lowers, and activating them raises, the probability of future movements; rapid signals in striatal dopamine axons can trigger locomotion (mouse)
pre-movement dopamine neuron activity relates to, and manipulating it changes, the vigour of future movements; dopamine depletion reduces vigor (mouse)
distinct dorsal striatal neuron classes represent vigor, and suppressing striatal activity during movement reduces it (mouse)
dorsolateral (not dorsomedial) striatum lesions keep actions sensitive to outcome devaluation: it is necessary for habit formation (rat)
start/stop activity emerges in nigrostriatal circuits during sequence learning, and both striatal pathways are needed to initiate and execute learned sequences (mouse)
arkypallidal neurons respond early and selectively to Stop cues, proposed to cancel actions in preparation via their projection to striatum (rat)

muscimol in the pars reticulata, releasing collicular cells from its tonic inhibition, causes irrepressible saccades and most disrupts saccades to remembered targets; suggested to apply to skeletal movements too (monkey)
a mutation in its gene occurs in families with autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease, and it forms the major filamentous component of Lewy bodies
loss of nigral dopamine neurons underlies the disease and causes deficits in movement initiation and slowness of movement
links.note: MPTP, which caused marked parkinsonism in people who injected it, is proposed to damage substantia nigra cells selectively (langston1983).

links.rel: excess subthalamic activity is implicated: lesioning the nucleus reduces akinesia, rigidity and tremor in MPTP-treated monkeys
classic model: changes in striatal projection neuron subpopulations that increase basal ganglia output are hypothesized to cause hypokinetic disorders
classic model: hyperkinetic disorders are postulated to result from selective impairment of striatal neurons projecting to the lateral pallidum
off medication, subthalamic and internal pallidal potentials are dominated by coherent activity below 30 Hz (four patients)
reduces subthalamic–pallidal activity below 30 Hz and brings a new peak near 70 Hz (four patients)
reduces symptoms; in early disease parkinsonism worsened less than with placebo over 42 weeks, but whether levodopa alters progression is uncertain (RCT)
links.note: Striatal dopamine-transporter uptake declined more with levodopa than with placebo, which may mean faster loss of nigrostriatal terminals or a pharmacologic effect on the transporter (fahn2004). In many patients, treatment is complicated by fluctuations between off and on periods, often with debilitating dyskinesias (limousin1998).

links.rel: subthalamic or pallidal stimulation improves motor function and quality of life more than best medical therapy (RCTs), with more serious adverse events
links.note: Stimulating only when local field potentials from the electrodes show pathological activity (adaptive DBS) beat continuous stimulation, with 56 percent less stimulation time, in 8 patients (little2013).

links.rel: therapeutic effects within the subthalamic nucleus can be accounted for by selective stimulation of afferent axons projecting to it (parkinsonian rodents)
an expanded, unstable CAG repeat in IT15 on 4p16.3, found on disease chromosomes in all 75 families examined
enkephalin-containing striatal neurons projecting to the external pallidum are much more affected in early and middle stages than substance P neurons projecting to the internal pallidum (post-mortem)
links.note: albin1989 postulates that hyperkinetic disorders result from selective impairment of striatal neurons projecting to the lateral pallidum.

links.rel: perforant path: entorhinal layer II gives rise to the major excitatory input to the hippocampus, which reaches the dentate gyrus first in the trisynaptic pathway
